The Diary Beside the Declaration

STS-HS11-L2-13001400-HSELA1112-HJD-MNA-01 • HS English 11-12 • Foundational U.S. Documents: Themes, Purposes, and Rhetorical Features
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Historical journals let a reader stand inside a moment instead of reading about it. Layla, Tarek, and Rania are pairing invented diary entries from a family who arrived from Beirut and Casablanca with the exact lines those readers met for the first time in English. A diary says I felt. The Declaration says we hold.
Which one persuades a stranger more, and what does each one want from its reader?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Layla doing?
Look at the picture. Can you describe what Layla is doing in one complete sentence using exact words instead of general words like thing or stuff?
2

Look at the picture. Can you describe what Tarek has in his hands in one complete sentence using exact words instead of general words like thing or stuff?
3

Look at the picture. Can you describe what the teacher is doing in one complete sentence using exact words instead of general words like thing or stuff?
4

Look at the picture. Can you describe what kind of room this is in one complete sentence using exact words instead of general words like thing or stuff?
5

Look at the picture. Can you describe what is on the big wall in one complete sentence using exact words instead of general words like thing or stuff?
6
What is Rania wearing?
Look at the picture. Can you describe what Rania has on in one complete sentence using exact words instead of general words like thing or stuff?
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
